            "audit_checkpoint": dict(self.audit_checkpoint),
        }
        # The rotatable checkpoint key and every retained public key live in
        # the state section (not a new top-level key) and are persisted in the
        # same atomic document as the checkpoint they authenticate.
        if audit_signer_state is not None:
            data["state"]["audit_signer"] = audit_signer_state
            data["state"]["audit_signer_history"] = [
                dict(entry) for entry in self.audit_signer_history
            ]
        # Only persist a forks section when candidates exist so a chain with
        # no forks keeps the canonical snapshot layout; loads default to [].
        if self.forks:
            data["forks"] = [
                [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
                for fork in sorted(self.forks.values(), key=lambda f: f[-1].block_hash)
            ]
        # Sync metadata is persisted in the same atomic document as the
        # candidate chains it references. A range-sync record additionally
        # stores its delivered {anchor, blocks} payload so same-key retries
        # stay replayable (and re-verifiable) without re-splicing against a
        # canonical chain that may have since advanced.
        if self.syncs:
            data["syncs"] = [
                {
                    "source": key[0],
                    "request_id": key[1],
                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
                    "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
                    "height": rec.get("height"),
                    "length": rec.get("length"),
                    "status": rec.get("status"),
                    **(
                        {"range": rec["range"]}
                        if rec.get("range") is not None
                        else {}
                    ),
                }
                for key, rec in sorted(self.syncs.items())
            ]
        # Signature-attested sync records live in their own section (and
        # idempotency namespace), each additionally carrying the frozen
        # attestation (signing public key, registry version, signature and the
        # candidate in its signed original form).
        if self.attested_syncs:
            data["attested_syncs"] = [
                {
                    "source": key[0],
                    "request_id": key[1],
                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
                    "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
                    "height": rec.get("height"),
                    "length": rec.get("length"),
                    "status": rec.get("status"),
                    "attested": rec["attested"],
                }
                for key, rec in sorted(self.attested_syncs.items())
            ]
        # Persistent source-trust registry and the keyless allowlist are part
        # of the same atomic document as every state change they describe.
        if self.trust_sources:
            data["trust_sources"] = [
                {"source": source, **self.trust_sources[source]}
                for source in sorted(self.trust_sources)
            ]
        # The per-source public-key history is persisted in the same atomic
        # document as the registry and the audit events it is reconstructed
        # from: one entry per registered source, keys ascending by version.
        if self.source_key_history:
            data["source_key_history"] = [
                {
                    "source": source,
                    "keys": [dict(entry) for entry in self.source_key_history[source]],
                }
                for source in sorted(self.source_key_history)
            ]
        if self.allowlist:
            data["allowlist"] = dict(sorted(self.allowlist.items()))
        # The audit trail is append-only; every trust change and every sync
        # reception/adoption/expiry is recorded here in write order.
        if self.audit_events:
            data["audit_events"] = list(self.audit_events)
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or "."
        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
        # Hold the class-wide recovery lock while a .ledger-* snapshot exists
        # on disk, so a concurrent in-process LedgerStore construction cannot
        # scan a half-written promotion.
        with self._recovery_lock:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                prefix=SNAPSHOT_PREFIX,
                suffix=f".gen{next_generation}",
                dir=directory,
            )
            promoted = False
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                    json.dump(data, fh, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)
                    fh.flush()
                    os.fsync(fh.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, self.path)
                promoted = True
                self._fsync_dir(directory)
                # Promotion is durable: now publish the prospective derived
                # views and advance the generation, together and last, so a
                # successful write is the only thing that changes memory.
                self.tx_index = next_index
                self.accounts = next_accounts
                self.generation = next_generation
            finally:
                if not promoted and os.path.exists(tmp_path):
                    # Promotion never happened: drop the half-written candidate so
                    # it cannot masquerade as a recoverable snapshot. A candidate
                    # written and fsynced *before* a crash during replace survives
                    # precisely because that crash skips this cleanup.
                    try:
                        os.unlink(tmp_path)
                    except OSError:
                        pass

    @staticmethod
    def _fsync_dir(directory: str) -> None:
        """Best-effort directory fsync so a rename survives a power loss."""
        try:
            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", 0))
        except OSError:
            return
        try:
            os.fsync(dir_fd)
        except OSError:
            pass
        finally:
            os.close(dir_fd)

    # -- chain helpers --------------------------------------------------------

    def tip(self) -> Block:
        return self.chain[-1]

    def tip_hash(self) -> str:
        return self.chain[-1].block_hash

    def next_height(self) -> int:
        return self.chain[-1].height + 1

    def tip_is_pending(self) -> bool:
        return self.chain[-1].status == STATUS_PENDING

    def block_at(self, height: int) -> Block | None:
        if 0 <= height < len(self.chain) and self.chain[height].height == height:
            return self.chain[height]
        return None

    def rollback_tip(self) -> Block:
        """Remove the pending tip block and return its transactions to the mempool.

        Transactions are restored de-duplicated: an id already present in the
        pending set (resubmitted while the block was unconfirmed) is kept as
        is, not overwritten. Caller must hold the lock and must have checked
        that the tip is a pending block. Does not save; callers persist.
        """
        block = self.chain.pop()
        for tx in block.transactions:
            self.pending.setdefault(tx.tx_id, tx)
        return block

1	"""Append-only audit log hash chaining, checkpoints and offline verification.
2	
3	Every audit event carries two SHA-256 links:
4	
5	* ``prev_hash``  — the previous event's ``event_hash``; 64 ASCII zeroes for
6	  the first event;
7	* ``event_hash`` — ``sha256(prev_hash ASCII || canonical-event UTF-8)`` where
8	  the canonical event is the event with both hash fields removed, serialized
9	  as sorted-key compact JSON (``sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")``,
10	  non-ASCII characters emitted as raw UTF-8).
11	
12	``audit_checkpoint`` is ``{"event_id", "event_hash"}`` pinning the latest
13	event: a fresh/empty log checks at ``{0, "0"*64}``. Offline verification walks
14	one or more exported pages, checking each page anchor, the dense event ids and
15	every link, and requires every page to pin the identical checkpoint with the
16	final page's last event (or the empty log) matching it.
17	
18	A page may additionally carry ``checkpoint_auth`` — an Ed25519 signature over
19	``SHA256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of {genesis_hash, checkpoint,
20	key_version})``. ``verify_export(document, trust)`` only checks that envelope
21	when a trust document (``genesis_hash`` plus a version-ascending
22	``audit_signers`` list) is supplied; authentication failures then use the
23	``auth`` error category.
24	"""
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	import hashlib
28	import json
29	
30	from . import crypto
31	
32	# Sentinel previous hash of the first audit event (and checkpoint of an empty
33	# log): 64 ASCII zeroes.
34	ZERO_HASH = "0" * 64
35	
36	# Names of the two link fields excluded from the hashed canonical event.
37	HASH_FIELDS = ("prev_hash", "event_hash")
38	
39	# Public offline-verification error categories.
40	ERR_INPUT = "input"
41	ERR_INTEGRITY = "integrity"
42	ERR_AUTH = "auth"
43	
44	
45	class AuditChainError(ValueError):
46	    """A persisted audit hash chain or checkpoint failed strict validation.
47	
48	    Carries a human-readable ``reason``; the persistence layer maps it onto a
49	    ``StateRecoveryError`` tagged with the offending snapshot path.
50	    """
51	
52	    def __init__(self, reason: str) -> None:
53	        self.reason = reason
54	        super().__init__(reason)
55	
56	
57	class _VerifyError(Exception):
58	    """Internal control-flow exception carrying the public error category."""
59	
60	    def __init__(self, category: str) -> None:
61	        self.category = category
62	        super().__init__(category)
63	
64	
65	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
66	    """Plain integer test; booleans are rejected (bool subclasses int)."""
67	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
68	
69	
70	def canonical_event(event: dict) -> bytes:
71	    """Sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON of the event with both hash fields removed.
72	
73	    This is the exact byte document chained into ``event_hash``; stripping the
74	    links makes the hash independent of any re-serialization of the stored
75	    event object.
76	    """
77	    stripped = {key: value for key, value in event.items() if key not in HASH_FIELDS}
78	    return json.dumps(
79	        stripped, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
80	    ).encode("utf-8")

83	def event_hash(prev_hash: str, event: dict) -> str:
84	    """SHA-256 hex of ``prev_hash`` ASCII bytes followed by the canonical event."""
85	    return hashlib.sha256(prev_hash.encode("ascii") + canonical_event(event)).hexdigest()
86	
87	
88	def link_events(events: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
89	    """Return copies of ``events`` with dense ids and fresh hash links.
90	
91	    Event ids are renumbered 1..N; the first event gets the all-zero
92	    ``prev_hash`` and every later event links to its predecessor. Does not
93	    mutate the input.
94	    """
95	    linked: list[dict] = []
96	    prev_hash = ZERO_HASH
97	    for index, event in enumerate(events):
98	        linked_event = dict(event)
99	        linked_event["event_id"] = index + 1
100	        linked_event["prev_hash"] = prev_hash
101	        linked_event["event_hash"] = event_hash(prev_hash, linked_event)
102	        linked.append(linked_event)
103	        prev_hash = linked_event["event_hash"]
104	    return linked

106	
107	def make_checkpoint(events: list[dict]) -> dict:
108	    """``{"event_id", "event_hash"}`` pinning the last event (or the zero root)."""
109	    if events:
110	        return {
111	            "event_id": len(events),
112	            "event_hash": events[-1]["event_hash"],
113	        }
114	    return {"event_id": 0, "event_hash": ZERO_HASH}

117	# Fields of a page's checkpoint authentication envelope.
118	AUTH_FIELDS = ("key_version", "signature")

121	def checkpoint_auth_object(
122	    genesis_hash: str, checkpoint: dict, key_version: int
123	) -> dict:
124	    """The exact JSON object covered by a checkpoint authentication signature.
125	
126	    ``{"genesis_hash", "checkpoint": {"event_id", "event_hash"},
127	    "key_version"}`` — the genesis anchor pins the deployment, the checkpoint
128	    pins the audit log head and the key version selects the verifying public
129	    key.
130	    """
131	    return {
132	        "genesis_hash": genesis_hash,
133	        "checkpoint": {

135	            "event_hash": checkpoint["event_hash"],

142	    """Sorted-key compact UTF-8 JSON of a checkpoint authentication object."""
143	    return json.dumps(
144	        auth_object, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
145	    ).encode("utf-8")

149	    private_key_hex: str, genesis_hash: str, checkpoint: dict, key_version: int

152

154	    """
155	    auth_object = checkpoint_auth_object(genesis_hash, checkpoint, key_version)
156	    digest = hashlib.sha256(checkpoint_auth_bytes(auth_object)).digest()
157	    return crypto.sign_message(private_key_hex, digest)

161	    public_key_hex: str,
162	    genesis_hash: str,
163	    checkpoint: dict,
164	    key_version: int,
165	    signature_hex: str,
166	) -> bool:

168	    auth_object = checkpoint_auth_object(genesis_hash, checkpoint, key_version)
169	    digest = hashlib.sha256(checkpoint_auth_bytes(auth_object)).digest()
170	    return crypto.verify_signature(public_key_hex, digest, signature_hex)

173	def validate_event_chain(events: object) -> None:
174	    """Strictly validate a persisted event list's dense ids and hash links.
175	
176	    ``event_id`` values must be exactly 1..N; each ``prev_hash`` must equal the
177	    previous event's ``event_hash`` (all zeroes for the first event) and every
178	    ``event_hash`` must recompute from the event with both hash fields removed.
179	    Raises AuditChainError on the first defect.
180	    """
181	    if not isinstance(events, list):
182	        raise AuditChainError("'audit_events' must be a list")
183	    prev_hash = ZERO_HASH
184	    for index, event in enumerate(events):
185	        event_id = index + 1
186	        if not isinstance(event, dict):
187	            raise AuditChainError(f"audit event {event_id} must be an object")
188	        if not _is_plain_int(event.get("event_id")) or event["event_id"] != event_id:

211	    """Validate an ``audit_checkpoint`` against the recovered event list.
212	
213	    It must be ``{"event_id": N, "event_hash": H}`` with N the (non-negative)
214	    number of events and H the last event's hash, or the all-zero root when the
215	    log is empty. Raises AuditChainError on any defect.
216	    """
217	    if not isinstance(checkpoint, dict):
218	        raise AuditChainError("'audit_checkpoint' must be an object")
219	    event_id = checkpoint.get("event_id")
220	    event_hash_value = checkpoint.get("event_hash")

235	def verify_export(document: object, trust: object = None) -> dict:
236	    """Offline-verify one audit export page or an ordered list of pages.
237	
238	    A page has the server shape
239	    ``{items, total, next_cursor, anchor_hash, checkpoint}``. Every page
240	    must pin the identical checkpoint, each page anchor must equal the
241	    running predecessor hash, item event ids must be dense and consecutive
242	    across pages, every ``prev_hash``/``event_hash`` pair must recompute,
243	    pagination counters must be self-consistent and the last page's tail
244	    must equal that shared checkpoint.
245	
246	    When ``trust`` is None (the default) no authentication is attempted and
247	    the behaviour is unchanged. When a trust document is supplied it must
248	    carry ``genesis_hash`` and a version-ascending ``audit_signers`` list
249	    (``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}``); every page must then
250	    carry the same ``checkpoint_auth`` envelope
251	    (``{key_version, signature}``) binding the same checkpoint, the key
252	    version must be known and activated at or before the checkpoint, and the
253	    Ed25519 signature over
254	    ``SHA256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of {genesis_hash, checkpoint,
255	    key_version})`` must verify against that version's public key.

257	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "checkpoint": {...}}`` or
258	    ``{"ok": False, "error": "input" | "integrity" | "auth"}``. Never raises
259	    for malformed input.

262	        pages = _coerce_pages(document)
263	        checkpoint = _verify_pages(pages)
264	        if trust is not None:
265	            _verify_checkpoint_auth(pages, checkpoint, trust)
266	    except _VerifyError as failure:
267	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
268	    except Exception:

270	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
271	    return {"ok": True, "checkpoint": checkpoint}

275	    """Normalize a single page object / list of pages, validating basic shape."""
276	    if isinstance(document, dict):
277	        pages = [document]
278	    elif isinstance(document, list) and (
279	        not document or all(isinstance(page, dict) for page in document)
280	    ):
281	        pages = document
282	    else:
283	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
284	    if not pages:
285	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
286	    return pages

289	def _parse_page_shape(page: object) -> dict:
290	    """Validate a page's structural fields; returns the dict on success."""
291	    if not isinstance(page, dict):
292	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
293	    for field in ("items", "total", "next_cursor", "anchor_hash", "checkpoint"):
294	        if field not in page:
295	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
296	    items = page["items"]
297	    total = page["total"]
298	    next_cursor = page["next_cursor"]
299	    anchor_hash = page["anchor_hash"]
300	    checkpoint = page["checkpoint"]
301	    if not isinstance(items, list):
302	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
303	    if not _is_plain_int(total) or total < 0:
304	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
305	    if next_cursor is not None and (not _is_plain_int(next_cursor) or next_cursor < 0):
306	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
307	    if not crypto.is_hex64(anchor_hash):
308	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
309	    if not isinstance(checkpoint, dict):
310	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
311	    checkpoint_id = checkpoint.get("event_id")
312	    checkpoint_hash = checkpoint.get("event_hash")
313	    if not _is_plain_int(checkpoint_id) or checkpoint_id < 0:
314	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
315	    if not crypto.is_hex64(checkpoint_hash):
316	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
317	    return page

320	def _verify_pages(pages: list[dict]) -> dict:
321	    """Walk every page in order; return the shared checkpoint on success."""
322	    running_id = 0
323	    running_hash = ZERO_HASH
324	    first_checkpoint: dict | None = None
325	    for page in pages:
326	        page = _parse_page_shape(page)
327	        items = page["items"]
328	        total = page["total"]
329	        next_cursor = page["next_cursor"]
330	        checkpoint = page["checkpoint"]
331	
332	        # Every page of one export pins the identical checkpoint; a replaced
333	        # or regressed checkpoint on any page breaks the export as a whole.
334	        if first_checkpoint is None:
335	            first_checkpoint = checkpoint
336	        elif checkpoint != first_checkpoint:
337	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
338	        # The export is unfiltered, so a page's total is the log length its
339	        # checkpoint was taken over.
340	        if checkpoint["event_id"] != total:
341	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
342	        # This page begins exactly where verification currently stands: the
343	        # declared anchor is the predecessor hash of its first item (or of the
344	        # cursor position for an empty page).
345	        if page["anchor_hash"] != running_hash:
346	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
347	
348	        for item in items:
349	            if not isinstance(item, dict):
350	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
351	            event_id = item.get("event_id")
352	            prev_hash = item.get("prev_hash")
353	            stored_hash = item.get("event_hash")
354	            if not _is_plain_int(event_id):
355	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
356	            if not crypto.is_hex64(prev_hash) or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_hash):
357	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
358	            if event_id != running_id + 1:
359	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
360	            if prev_hash != running_hash:
361	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
362	            if event_hash(running_hash, item) != stored_hash:
363	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
364	            running_id = event_id
365	            running_hash = stored_hash
366	
367	        # Pagination self-consistency: a non-null next_cursor continues exactly
368	        # after this page and stays below total; a server page with limit >= 1
369	        # is therefore non-empty whenever it is not the last page. A null
370	        # next_cursor ends exactly at the total.
371	        if next_cursor is None:
372	            if running_id != total:
373	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
374	        else:
375	            if not items or next_cursor != running_id or next_cursor >= total:
376	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
377	
378	    # The final page must end exactly on the checkpoint every page pinned.
379	    assert first_checkpoint is not None
380	    if (
381	        running_id != first_checkpoint["event_id"]
382	        or running_hash != first_checkpoint["event_hash"]
383	    ):
384	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
385	    return dict(first_checkpoint)
386	
387	
388	def _parse_trust_signers(trust: object) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict]]:
389	    """Strictly parse a trust document's genesis anchor and audit signers.
390	
391	    Returns ``(genesis_hash, {version: {public_key, activated_event_id}})``.
392	    Versions must be dense and ascending starting at 1, the first
393	    ``activated_event_id`` must be 0 and later activation ids must be strictly
394	    ascending. Any defect is an input error.
395	    """
396	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
397	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
398	    genesis_hash = trust.get("genesis_hash")
399	    if not crypto.is_hex64(genesis_hash):
400	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
401	    raw_signers = trust.get("audit_signers")
402	    if not isinstance(raw_signers, list) or not raw_signers:
403	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
404	    signers: dict[int, dict] = {}
405	    previous_activated: int | None = None
406	    for position, entry in enumerate(raw_signers):
407	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
408	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
409	        version = entry.get("version")
410	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
411	        activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
412	        if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != position + 1:
413	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
414	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
415	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
416	        if not _is_plain_int(activated) or activated < 0:
417	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
418	        if position == 0:
419	            if activated != 0:
420	                raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
421	        elif activated <= previous_activated:
422	            # A gap in versions is already rejected above; an activation id
423	            # that retreats (or stands still) is likewise a malformed list.
424	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
425	        previous_activated = activated
426	        signers[version] = {
427	            "public_key": public_key,
428	            "activated_event_id": activated,
429	        }
430	    return genesis_hash, signers

432	
433	def _verify_checkpoint_auth(
434	    pages: list[dict], checkpoint: dict, trust: object
435	) -> None:
436	    """Verify the Ed25519 checkpoint authentication carried by every page.
437	
438	    Every page must carry the same ``checkpoint_auth`` envelope
439	    (``{key_version, signature}``) and pin the same checkpoint; the key
440	    version must identify a signer already activated at or before the
441	    checkpoint and the signature must verify over
442	    ``SHA256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of {genesis_hash, checkpoint,
443	    key_version})`` under the trust document's anchor. Structural defects are
444	    input errors; missing, unknown-version, cross-page-inconsistent or
445	    cryptographically invalid authentication is an auth error; a page whose
446	    checkpoint differs from the verified head is an integrity error.
447	    """
448	    genesis_hash, signers = _parse_trust_signers(trust)
449	    envelopes: list[object] = []
450	    for page in pages:
451	        if page.get("checkpoint") != checkpoint:
452	            # Two pages of one export must pin the same log head.
453	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INTEGRITY)
454	        envelope = page.get("checkpoint_auth")
455	        if envelope is None:
456	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_AUTH)
457	        if not isinstance(envelope, dict):
458	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
459	        key_version = envelope.get("key_version")
460	        signature = envelope.get("signature")
461	        if not _is_plain_int(key_version) or key_version < 1:
462	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
463	        if not isinstance(signature, str) or not crypto.is_hex128(signature):
464	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
465	        envelopes.append({"key_version": key_version, "signature": signature})
466	
467	    first = envelopes[0]
468	    for envelope in envelopes[1:]:
469	        if envelope != first:
470	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_AUTH)
471	
472	    signer = signers.get(first["key_version"])
473	    if signer is None:
474	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_AUTH)
475	    # A trust document may not describe signer activations that lie beyond the
476	    # checkpoint head it is meant to authenticate. The *selected* key's own
477	    # activation beyond the head is reported as auth (an unactivated key
478	    # version, matching the signed-envelope failure category); any other
479	    # history entry beyond the head makes the document itself inconsistent
480	    # with the verified checkpoint and is an input error.
481	    for other_version, entry in signers.items():
482	        if other_version == first["key_version"]:
483	            continue
484	        if entry["activated_event_id"] > checkpoint["event_id"]:
485	            raise _VerifyError(ERR_INPUT)
486	    # A signer can only authenticate a checkpoint taken at or after the event
487	    # that activated its key.
488	    if checkpoint["event_id"] < signer["activated_event_id"]:
489	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_AUTH)
490	    if not verify_checkpoint_auth(
491	        signer["public_key"],
492	        genesis_hash,
493	        checkpoint,
494	        first["key_version"],
495	        first["signature"],
496	    ):
497	        raise _VerifyError(ERR_AUTH)

1	"""Offline whole-snapshot consistency verification.
2	
3	``verify_snapshot(document)`` re-derives every self-contained invariant of a
4	persisted ledger snapshot without contacting a server or touching the
5	filesystem::
6	
7	    {
8	      "state":             object (generation, optional state_root, ...),
9	      "chain":             non-empty block list starting at genesis,
10	      "pending":           mempool transaction list,
11	      "index":             {tx_id: confirmed_height},
12	      "accounts":          {account: {sent, received, transactions}},
13	      "audit_checkpoint":  {"event_id", "event_hash"},
14	      "audit_events":      optional append-only hash-chained event list,
15	      # trust extensions, verified when present (a pre-feature snapshot
16	      # omits them and is accepted as legacy):
17	      "trust_sources" / "allowlist" / "source_key_history",
18	      # extensions, accepted but not re-verified here:
19	      "forks" / "syncs" / "attested_syncs",
20	    }
21	
22	Verification recomputes, from the raw JSON values:
23	
24	* every transaction's canonical ``tx_id`` and Ed25519 signature;
25	* every block's ascending tx_id order, Merkle root and block hash, the
26	  consecutive heights and ``prev_hash`` linkage back to the all-zero anchor,
27	  the confirmed/empty genesis rules and the pending-only-at-tip rule;
28	* mempool uniqueness and the mempool/chain de-duplication;
29	* the confirmed-only transaction ``index`` and ``accounts`` activity;
30	* the confirmed-account Merkle ``state_root`` (using ``state.initial_balance``
31	  when recorded, else the default endowment);
32	* when ``audit_events`` is present, its dense event ids and SHA-256 hash links
33	  plus the ``audit_checkpoint`` pinning the log head (an absent event list
34	  still requires the empty-log checkpoint ``{0, "0"*64}``);
35	* when the trust extensions are present: ``trust_sources`` as a
36	  source-ascending unique array of ``{source, public_key, expires_at,
37	  version, status}`` records (64-char lowercase hex key, non-boolean integer
38	  expiry, positive integer version, ``active``/``revoked`` status),
39	  ``allowlist`` as a ``source -> non-boolean integer expires_at`` object, and
40	  ``source_key_history`` as a source-ascending array of ``{source, keys}``
41	  items whose ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` keys are dense
42	  from version 1 with strictly ascending, positive activation ids —
43	  bidirectionally consistent with the trust registry's latest
44	  version/public key/revoked status and with the audit log's source-key
45	  lifecycle events (``source_registered`` opens version 1,
46	  ``source_rotated`` increments it, ``source_revoked`` pins the current key
47	  and must be present exactly when the registry record is ``revoked``);
48	  every registry source, history item and lifecycle event must correspond
49	  both ways, so an orphan source or event and a missing event are integrity
50	  failures. A snapshot predating ``source_key_history`` omits the section and
51	  is accepted as legacy without that cross-check.
52	
53	Two failure categories are returned, never raised:
54	
55	* ``input`` — the document is not an object, a required section is missing or
56	  has the wrong JSON type, an unknown top-level key appears, or a field carries
57	  a non-integer/non-string value of the wrong kind before any recomputation
58	  (including a trust record missing or adding a key), or a trust extension
59	  array is out of its declared order (``trust_sources`` items not
60	  source-ascending, ``source_key_history`` items not source-ascending, or
61	  ``keys`` items whose versions are not dense from 1 with strictly ascending
62	  activation ids);
63	* ``integrity`` — the document parses but a recomputed value disagrees with
64	  the stored one (tx/merkle/block hashes, linkage, index, accounts, state_root,
65	  pending uniqueness or the audit chain/checkpoint), or the trust extensions
66	  disagree among themselves, the registry or the audit event log (an invalid
67	  public key or status, a non-positive version, a non-positive activation id,
68	  an orphan source or lifecycle event, a missing lifecycle event, or a
69	  revoked-status mismatch).

358	            # stored block document cannot represent the recomputed block.
359	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None

363	def _parse_transaction(tx_raw: object) -> Transaction:
364	    """Validate one raw transaction document and recompute tx_id/signature.
365	
366	    Missing keys or non-plain-integer/non-string field types (including a
367	    non-positive amount) are input errors; a recomputed tx_id or Ed25519
368	    signature mismatch is an integrity error.
369	    """
370	    if not isinstance(tx_raw, dict):
371	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

373	        if key not in tx_raw:
374	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
375	    sender = tx_raw["from"]
376	    recipient = tx_raw["to"]
377	    amount = tx_raw["amount"]
378	    signature = tx_raw["signature"]
379	    stored_tx_id = tx_raw["tx_id"]
380	    if not isinstance(sender, str) or not isinstance(recipient, str):
381	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
382	    if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
383	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
384	    if not isinstance(signature, str) or not isinstance(stored_tx_id, str):
385	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
386	    try:
387	        tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
388	    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
389	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT) from None
390	    if stored_tx_id != tx.tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
391	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
392	    if not crypto.verify_signature(tx.sender, tx.message, tx.signature):
393	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

397	def _verify_pending(pending_raw: list, chain_tx_ids: set[str]) -> None:
398	    """Mempool entries are well-formed, unique, and disjoint from the chain."""
399	    pending: set[str] = set()
400	    for tx_raw in pending_raw:
401	        tx = _parse_transaction(tx_raw)
402	        if tx.tx_id in pending:
403	            # Duplicate pending transaction in the mempool.
404	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

406	            # A mempool transaction already sealed into a block.
407	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

412	    blocks: list[Block],
413	) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, dict]]:

418	    an artifact the node itself wrote.

427	            for account in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
428	                entry = accounts.setdefault(
429	                    account, {"sent": 0, "received": 0, "transactions": []}
430	                )
431	                entry["transactions"].append(tx.tx_id)
432	            accounts[tx.sender]["sent"] += tx.amount
433	            accounts[tx.recipient]["received"] += tx.amount
434	    return tx_index, accounts

497	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

507	    allowlist_raw: object,
508	    history_raw: object,
509	    events: list[dict],
510	) -> None:
511	    """Validate the trust extension sections against each other and the log.
512	
513	    Every section is optional (a pre-feature snapshot omits them); a present
514	    section is strictly validated. Field presence and raw JSON primitive types
515	    are input errors; value-format, ordering and uniqueness defects, and any
516	    disagreement between the key history, the trust registry and the audit
517	    log's source-key lifecycle events, are integrity errors.
518	
519	    The registry is always reconciled against the event log: every registry
520	    source must have a complete, well-formed lifecycle (register -> rotates ->
521	    at most one revoke), its latest version/public key and its revoked status
522	    must agree with the log, and every lifecycle event must name a registry
523	    source — orphan sources/events and missing events are integrity failures.
524	    A snapshot predating ``source_key_history`` omits that one section: the
525	    registry/event checks still run, but there is no persisted history array to
526	    cross-check (the history is reconstructed in memory by the node instead).

530	    expected = _reconstruct_key_history(registry, events)
531	    if history_raw is None:

538	        if source not in registry:
539	            # A history item whose source is absent from the registry is
540	            # orphan data; the persisted sections must agree bidirectionally.
541	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

550	def _parse_trust_sources(raw: object) -> dict[str, dict]:
551	    """Validate the persisted source-trust registry as a raw JSON array.
552	
553	    The array must be sorted by source with no duplicates; each record
554	    carries exactly ``{source, public_key, expires_at, version, status}``.
555	    A missing/extra key, a wrong primitive field type or an
556	    unsorted/duplicate source is an input error; an invalid public key or
557	    status, or a non-positive integer version, is an integrity error.
558	    """

560	        return {}
561	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
562	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
563	    registry: dict[str, dict] = {}
564	    previous: str | None = None
565	    for entry in raw:
566	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
567	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

569	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

571	        public_key = entry["public_key"]
572	        expires_at = entry["expires_at"]
573	        version = entry["version"]
574	        status = entry["status"]
575	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
576	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
577	        if not isinstance(public_key, str):
578	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
579	        if not _is_int(expires_at):
580	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
581	        if not _is_int(version):
582	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
583	        if not isinstance(status, str):
584	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
585	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
586	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
587	        if version < 1:
588	            # A structurally integer but non-positive version is a corrupt
589	            # value, not a wrong-shape document.
590	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
591	        if status not in _TRUST_STATUSES:
592	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
593	        if previous is not None and source <= previous:
594	            # Sources must be unique and strictly ascending; an out-of-order
595	            # item is a key-order (shape) defect, not a value mismatch.
596	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
597	        previous = source
598	        registry[source] = {
599	            "public_key": public_key,
600	            "expires_at": expires_at,
601	            "version": version,
602	            "status": status,

608	    """Validate the keyless ``{source: expires_at}`` allowlist object."""

610	        return
611	    if not isinstance(raw, dict):

620	def _parse_source_key_history(raw: object) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
621	    """Validate the persisted per-source key history structurally.
622	
623	    The array must be sorted by source with no duplicates; each item is
624	    exactly ``{source, keys}`` with a non-empty ``keys`` list of
625	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` entries whose versions are
626	    dense from 1 and whose activation ids are positive and strictly ascend.
627	    A missing/extra key, a wrong primitive field type, a duplicate/unsorted
628	    source, non-dense versions or non-ascending activation ids is an input
629	    error; an invalid public key, a non-positive version or a non-positive
630	    activation id is integrity.
631	    """
632	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
633	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
634	    history: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
635	    previous: str | None = None
636	    for item in raw:
637	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
638	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
639	        if set(item) != set(_HISTORY_ITEM_KEYS):
640	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
641	        source = item["source"]
642	        keys = item["keys"]
643	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
644	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
645	        if not isinstance(keys, list) or not keys:
646	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
647	        if previous is not None and source <= previous:
648	            # History items must be unique and source-ascending like the
649	            # registry they mirror; an out-of-order item is a key-order
650	            # (shape) defect, not a value mismatch.
651	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
652	        previous = source
653	        entries: list[dict] = []
654	        for position, entry in enumerate(keys):
655	            if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(_HISTORY_KEY_KEYS):

657	            version = entry["version"]
658	            public_key = entry["public_key"]
659	            activated = entry["activated_event_id"]
660	            if not _is_int(version):
661	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
662	            if not isinstance(public_key, str):
663	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
664	            if not _is_int(activated):
665	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
666	            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
667	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
668	            if version < 1:
669	                # A structurally integer but non-positive version is a corrupt
670	                # value, not a wrong-shape document.
671	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
672	            if version != position + 1:
673	                # Key versions are dense from 1; an out-of-order keys item is
674	                # a key-order (shape) defect, not a value mismatch.
675	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
676	            if activated < 1:

678	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
679	            if position > 0 and activated <= entries[-1]["activated_event_id"]:
680	                # Activation event ids strictly ascend with the version; an
681	                # out-of-order keys item is a key-order (shape) defect.
682	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
683	            entries.append(
684	                {
685	                    "version": version,
686	                    "public_key": public_key,

694	def _reconstruct_key_history(
695	    registry: dict[str, dict], events: list[dict]
696	) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
697	    """Rebuild the expected key histories and reconcile them with the registry.
698	
699	    Mirrors ``LedgerStore._reconstruct_source_key_history`` but enforces
700	    *bidirectional* correspondence among the registry, the persisted history
701	    and the audit log:
702	
703	    * every ``source_registered`` / ``source_rotated`` / ``source_revoked``
704	      event must name a source present in the registry (an event for an
705	      unknown source is an orphan event);
706	    * version 1 is activated by a source's single ``source_registered``
707	      event, each later version by the matching dense ``source_rotated``
708	      event, and a ``source_revoked`` event references the current key
709	      without adding one;
710	    * each registry source must have its registration (a missing event is
711	      fatal), the number of key events must equal its current version, the
712	      latest event's public key must equal the registry key, and the
713	      registry status is ``revoked`` exactly when a revoke event exists.
714	
715	    Any malformed lifecycle payload, orphan event, missing registration,
716	    version gap, rotation after revocation, latest-key/version disagreement
717	    or revoked-status mismatch is an integrity error. Returns the
718	    reconstructed histories.
719	    """
720	    # Collect every source-key lifecycle event by source in log order. A
721	    # lifecycle event for an unknown source is validated like any other; it
722	    # can never be silently ignored as an orphan.
723	    events_by_source: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
724	    for event in events:
725	        kind = event.get("kind")
726	        if kind not in _SOURCE_KEY_EVENT_KINDS:
727	            continue
728	        source = event.get("source")
729	        event_id = event.get("event_id")
730	        public_key = event.get("public_key")
731	        expires_at = event.get("expires_at")
732	        version = event.get("version")
733	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
734	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
735	        if (
736	            not isinstance(public_key, str)
737	            or not crypto.is_hex64(public_key)
738	            or not _is_int(expires_at)
739	            or not _is_int(version)
740	            or version < 1
741	            or not _is_int(event_id)
742	            or event_id < 1
743	        ):
744	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
745	        events_by_source.setdefault(source, []).append(event)
746	
747	    for source in events_by_source:
748	        if source not in registry:
749	            # A source-key lifecycle event with no registry record is orphan
750	            # data: the registry and the event log must correspond both ways.
751	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
752	
753	    reconstructed: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
754	    for source, record in registry.items():
755	        entries: list[dict] = []
756	        revoked = False
757	        next_version = 1
758	        for event in events_by_source.get(source, ()):
759	            kind = event["kind"]
760	            event_id = event["event_id"]
761	            public_key = event["public_key"]
762	            version = event["version"]
763	            if kind == EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED:
764	                if entries or version != 1:
765	                    # The history opens with a single version-1 registration.
766	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
767	                entries.append(
768	                    {
769	                        "version": 1,
770	                        "public_key": public_key,
771	                        "activated_event_id": event_id,
772	                    }
773	                )
774	                next_version = 2
775	            elif kind == EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED:
776	                if revoked or not entries or version != next_version:
777	                    # Rotations increment the version one step at a time and
778	                    # never happen after revocation.
779	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
780	                entries.append(
781	                    {
782	                        "version": version,
783	                        "public_key": public_key,
784	                        "activated_event_id": event_id,
785	                    }
786	                )
787	                next_version = version + 1
788	            else:  # EVENT_SOURCE_REVOKED
789	                if (
790	                    not entries
791	                    or version != entries[-1]["version"]
792	                    or public_key != entries[-1]["public_key"]
793	                ):
794	                    # Revocation pins the current key without adding one.
795	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
796	                revoked = True
797	        if not entries:
798	            # A registered source has no source_registered event.
799	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
800	        if len(entries) != record["version"]:
801	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
802	        if entries[-1]["public_key"] != record["public_key"]:
803	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
804	        if revoked != (record["status"] == TRUST_REVOKED):
805	            # The registry status and the event log must agree on whether the
806	            # source was revoked: a revoked record without a revoke event, or
807	            # an active record carrying one, is corruption.
808	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
809	        reconstructed[source] = entries
810	    return reconstructed
