"""Offline whole-snapshot consistency verification.

``verify_snapshot(document)`` re-derives every self-contained invariant of a
persisted ledger snapshot without contacting a server or touching the
filesystem::

    {
      "state":             object (generation, optional state_root, ...),
      "chain":             non-empty block list starting at genesis,
      "pending":           mempool transaction list,
      "index":             {tx_id: confirmed_height},
      "accounts":          {account: {sent, received, transactions}},
      "audit_checkpoint":  {"event_id", "event_hash"},
      "audit_events":      optional append-only hash-chained event list,
      # trust extensions, verified when present (a pre-feature snapshot
      # omits them and is accepted as legacy):
      "trust_sources" / "allowlist" / "source_key_history",
      # extensions, accepted but not re-verified here:
      "forks" / "syncs" / "attested_syncs",
    }

Verification recomputes, from the raw JSON values:

* every transaction's canonical ``tx_id`` and Ed25519 signature;
* every block's ascending tx_id order, Merkle root and block hash, the
  consecutive heights and ``prev_hash`` linkage back to the all-zero anchor,
  the confirmed/empty genesis rules and the pending-only-at-tip rule;
* mempool uniqueness and the mempool/chain de-duplication;
* the confirmed-only transaction ``index`` and ``accounts`` activity;
* the confirmed-account Merkle ``state_root`` (using ``state.initial_balance``
  when recorded, else the default endowment);
* when ``audit_events`` is present, its dense event ids and SHA-256 hash links
  plus the ``audit_checkpoint`` pinning the log head (an absent event list
  still requires the empty-log checkpoint ``{0, "0"*64}``);
* when the trust extensions are present: ``trust_sources`` as a
  source-ascending unique array of ``{source, public_key, expires_at,
  version, status}`` records (64-char lowercase hex key, non-boolean integer
  expiry, positive integer version, ``active``/``revoked`` status),
  ``allowlist`` as a ``source -> non-boolean integer expires_at`` object, and
  ``source_key_history`` as a source-ascending array of ``{source, keys}``
  items whose ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` keys are dense
  from version 1 with strictly ascending, positive activation ids —
  bidirectionally consistent with the trust registry's latest
  version/public key/revoked status and with the audit log's source-key
  lifecycle events (``source_registered`` opens version 1,
  ``source_rotated`` increments it, ``source_revoked`` pins the current key
  and must be present exactly when the registry record is ``revoked``);
  every registry source, history item and lifecycle event must correspond
  both ways, so an orphan source or event and a missing event are integrity
  failures. A snapshot predating ``source_key_history`` omits the section and
  is accepted as legacy without that cross-check.

Two failure categories are returned, never raised:

* ``input`` — the document is not an object, a required section is missing or
  has the wrong JSON type, an unknown top-level key appears, or a field carries
  a non-integer/non-string value of the wrong kind before any recomputation
  (including a trust record missing or adding a key), or a trust extension
  array is out of its declared order (``trust_sources`` items not
  source-ascending, ``source_key_history`` items not source-ascending, or
  ``keys`` items whose versions are not dense from 1 with strictly ascending
  activation ids);
* ``integrity`` — the document parses but a recomputed value disagrees with
  the stored one (tx/merkle/block hashes, linkage, index, accounts, state_root,
  pending uniqueness or the audit chain/checkpoint), or the trust extensions
  disagree among themselves, the registry or the audit event log (an invalid
  public key or status, a non-positive version, a non-positive activation id,
  an orphan source or lifecycle event, a missing lifecycle event, or a
  revoked-status mismatch).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from . import audit
from . import crypto
from .models import (
    STATUS_CONFIRMED,
    STATUS_PENDING,
    Block,
    Transaction,
    compute_block_hash,
)
from .store import (
    DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE,
    EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED,
    EVENT_SOURCE_REVOKED,
    EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED,
    GENESIS_PREV_HASH,
    TRUST_ACTIVE,
    TRUST_REVOKED,
    LedgerStore,
)

# Public error categories.
ERR_INPUT = "input"
ERR_INTEGRITY = "integrity"

# Required top-level sections; every one must be present with the right type.
REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ("state", "chain", "pending", "index", "accounts", "audit_checkpoint")

# Sections a snapshot may additionally carry. forks/syncs/attested_syncs are
# durable state but their own invariants are not part of this self-contained
# check; audit_events is optional because a pre-audit-chain snapshot omits it;
# the trust extensions are optional because a pre-feature snapshot omits them
# (each is strictly verified when present).
KNOWN_OPTIONAL_SECTIONS = (
    "audit_events",
    "forks",
    "syncs",
    "attested_syncs",
    "trust_sources",
    "allowlist",
    "source_key_history",
)

# Raw keys every stored block document must carry ("status" defaults to
# confirmed for legacy snapshots).
_BLOCK_KEYS = ("height", "prev_hash", "merkle_root", "block_hash", "transactions")

# Raw keys every stored transaction document must carry.
_TX_KEYS = ("from", "to", "amount", "signature", "tx_id")

# Exact key sets of the trust extension records.
_TRUST_SOURCE_KEYS = ("source", "public_key", "expires_at", "version", "status")
_TRUST_STATUSES = (TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED)
_HISTORY_ITEM_KEYS = ("source", "keys")
_HISTORY_KEY_KEYS = ("version", "public_key", "activated_event_id")

# Audit event kinds reconstructing a source's key history.
_SOURCE_KEY_EVENT_KINDS = (
    EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED,
    EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED,
    EVENT_SOURCE_REVOKED,
)


class _Failure(Exception):
    """Internal control-flow exception carrying the public error category."""

    def __init__(self, category: str) -> None:
        self.category = category
        super().__init__(category)


def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
    """Plain integer test; booleans are rejected (bool subclasses int)."""
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


def _failed(category: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "ok": False,
        "error": category,
        "generation": None,
        "height": None,
        "tip_hash": None,
        "state_root": None,
        "audit_checkpoint": None,
    }


def verify_snapshot(document: object) -> dict:
    """Verify the internal consistency of one decoded snapshot document.

    Returns ``{"ok": True, "error": None, "generation", "height", "tip_hash",
    "state_root", "audit_checkpoint"}`` on success, or the same shape with
    ``ok`` False, ``error`` set to ``"input"``/``"integrity"`` and every other
    field null. Never raises for malformed input.
    """
    try:
        if not isinstance(document, dict):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        result = _verify(document)
    except _Failure as failure:
        return _failed(failure.category)
    except Exception:
        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs report rather than crash.
        return _failed(ERR_INPUT)
    return {
        "ok": True,
        "error": None,
        "generation": result["generation"],
        "height": result["height"],
        "tip_hash": result["tip_hash"],
        "state_root": result["state_root"],
        "audit_checkpoint": result["audit_checkpoint"],
    }


def _verify(data: dict) -> dict:
    # Unknown top-level keys make the document shape wrong; the five
    # extension sections plus the optional audit log are the only extras.
    allowed = set(REQUIRED_SECTIONS) | set(KNOWN_OPTIONAL_SECTIONS)
    for key in data:
        if key not in allowed:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    for section in REQUIRED_SECTIONS:
        if section not in data:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

    state = data["state"]
    chain_raw = data["chain"]
    pending_raw = data["pending"]
    index_raw = data["index"]
    accounts_raw = data["accounts"]
    checkpoint_raw = data["audit_checkpoint"]

    # -- core section types --------------------------------------------------
    if not isinstance(state, dict):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if not isinstance(chain_raw, list) or not chain_raw:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if not isinstance(pending_raw, list):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if not isinstance(index_raw, dict):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if not isinstance(accounts_raw, dict):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

    generation = state.get("generation", 0)
    if not _is_int(generation) or generation < 0:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    endowment = state.get("initial_balance")
    if endowment is not None and (
        not _is_int(endowment) or endowment <= 0
    ):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if endowment is None:
        endowment = DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
    recorded_state_root = state.get("state_root")
    if recorded_state_root is not None and not isinstance(recorded_state_root, str):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

    # -- chain recomputation -------------------------------------------------
    blocks, seen_tx_ids = _recompute_chain(chain_raw)

    # -- mempool --------------------------------------------------------------
    _verify_pending(pending_raw, seen_tx_ids)

    tip = blocks[-1]
    if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
    if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
    if (
        state.get("tip_status") is not None
        and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
    ):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

    # -- derived index / accounts / state root -------------------------------
    expected_index, expected_accounts = _compute_derived(blocks)
    _verify_index(index_raw, expected_index)
    _verify_accounts(accounts_raw, expected_accounts)

    leaves = [
        crypto.account_state_leaf(account, balance, transactions)
        for account, balance, transactions in LedgerStore.account_state_rows(
            blocks, endowment
        )
    ]
    state_root = crypto.account_state_root(leaves)
    if recorded_state_root is not None:
        # A non-string was an input error above; a wrong-length/non-hex string
        # or a digest mismatch is corruption of the stored artifact.
        if not crypto.is_hex64(recorded_state_root) or recorded_state_root != state_root:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

    # -- audit hash chain and checkpoint -------------------------------------
    checkpoint, events = _verify_audit(data.get("audit_events"), checkpoint_raw)

    # -- trust extensions (registry, allowlist, key history) ------------------
    _verify_trust(
        data.get("trust_sources"),
        data.get("allowlist"),
        data.get("source_key_history"),
        events,
    )

    return {
        "generation": generation,
        "height": tip.height,
        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
        "state_root": state_root,
        "audit_checkpoint": checkpoint,
    }


def _recompute_chain(chain_raw: list) -> tuple[list[Block], set[str]]:
    """Parse and re-verify the canonical chain straight from the raw JSON.

    Field presence/type defects are input errors; every recomputed mismatch
    (heights, prev_hash links, tx_ids, signatures, ordering, Merkle roots,
    block hashes, genesis/pending-status rules) is an integrity error.
    """
    blocks: list[Block] = []
    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
    for position, block_raw in enumerate(chain_raw):
        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        for key in _BLOCK_KEYS:
            if key not in block_raw:
                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        height = block_raw["height"]
        prev_hash = block_raw["prev_hash"]
        merkle_root = block_raw["merkle_root"]
        block_hash = block_raw["block_hash"]
        txs_raw = block_raw["transactions"]
        status = block_raw.get("status", STATUS_CONFIRMED)
        # Raw types are checked before any use: a string/float/bool height or
        # amount is never coerced into the integer it resembles.
        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not isinstance(merkle_root, str) or not isinstance(block_hash, str):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not isinstance(status, str):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if status not in (STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_CONFIRMED):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

        if height != position:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        expected_prev = (
            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
        )
        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if position == 0 and (
            status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw
        ):
            # Genesis is born confirmed and carries no transactions.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if position < len(chain_raw) - 1 and status == STATUS_PENDING:
            # Pending blocks may only sit at the chain tip.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

        tx_ids: list[str] = []
        for tx_raw in txs_raw:
            tx = _parse_transaction(tx_raw)
            if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
            seen_tx_ids.add(tx.tx_id)
            tx_ids.append(tx.tx_id)

        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root) != block_hash:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        try:
            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            # Every field was validated above; reaching here still means the
            # stored block document cannot represent the recomputed block.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
    return blocks, seen_tx_ids


def _parse_transaction(tx_raw: object) -> Transaction:
    """Validate one raw transaction document and recompute tx_id/signature.

    Missing keys or non-plain-integer/non-string field types (including a
    non-positive amount) are input errors; a recomputed tx_id or Ed25519
    signature mismatch is an integrity error.
    """
    if not isinstance(tx_raw, dict):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    for key in _TX_KEYS:
        if key not in tx_raw:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    sender = tx_raw["from"]
    recipient = tx_raw["to"]
    amount = tx_raw["amount"]
    signature = tx_raw["signature"]
    stored_tx_id = tx_raw["tx_id"]
    if not isinstance(sender, str) or not isinstance(recipient, str):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if not isinstance(signature, str) or not isinstance(stored_tx_id, str):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    try:
        tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT) from None
    if stored_tx_id != tx.tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
    if not crypto.verify_signature(tx.sender, tx.message, tx.signature):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
    return tx


def _verify_pending(pending_raw: list, chain_tx_ids: set[str]) -> None:
    """Mempool entries are well-formed, unique, and disjoint from the chain."""
    pending: set[str] = set()
    for tx_raw in pending_raw:
        tx = _parse_transaction(tx_raw)
        if tx.tx_id in pending:
            # Duplicate pending transaction in the mempool.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if tx.tx_id in chain_tx_ids:
            # A mempool transaction already sealed into a block.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        pending.add(tx.tx_id)


def _compute_derived(
    blocks: list[Block],
) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, dict]]:
    """Confirmed-only tx_id -> height index and per-account activity.

    Mirrors ``LedgerStore._compute_derived`` exactly (including a self-send
    listing its tx_id once per side) so the comparison can never disagree on
    an artifact the node itself wrote.
    """
    tx_index: dict[str, int] = {}
    accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for block in blocks:
        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
            continue
        for tx in block.transactions:
            tx_index[tx.tx_id] = block.height
            for account in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
                entry = accounts.setdefault(
                    account, {"sent": 0, "received": 0, "transactions": []}
                )
                entry["transactions"].append(tx.tx_id)
            accounts[tx.sender]["sent"] += tx.amount
            accounts[tx.recipient]["received"] += tx.amount
    return tx_index, accounts


def _verify_index(raw: dict, expected: dict[str, int]) -> None:
    for key, value in raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not _is_int(value) or value < 0:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if raw != expected:
        # Any extra, missing or remapped confirmed-transaction entry is a
        # derived-data inconsistency.
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)


def _verify_accounts(raw: dict, expected: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
    for account, entry in raw.items():
        if not isinstance(account, str) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        sent = entry.get("sent")
        received = entry.get("received")
        transactions = entry.get("transactions")
        if not _is_int(sent) or not _is_int(received) or not isinstance(transactions, list):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if any(not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if raw != expected:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)


def _verify_audit(events_raw: object, checkpoint_raw: object) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]:
    """Validate the optional event hash chain and the mandatory checkpoint.

    A present ``audit_events`` section must be a list of objects whose dense
    1..N ids, prev_hash links and event_hash digests all recompute; the
    checkpoint (required even with no event list) must pin the recomputed log
    head, or the all-zero root for an empty log. Chain/checkpoint defects are
    integrity errors; the section/value types are input errors. Returns the
    checkpoint summary and the validated event list (empty when the section
    is absent) for the trust cross-checks.
    """
    if events_raw is None:
        events: list[dict] = []
    else:
        if not isinstance(events_raw, list):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if any(not isinstance(event, dict) for event in events_raw):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        events = events_raw
        try:
            audit.validate_event_chain(events)
        except audit.AuditChainError:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None

    if not isinstance(checkpoint_raw, dict):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if set(checkpoint_raw) != {"event_id", "event_hash"}:
        # The checkpoint is exactly {event_id, event_hash}; any extra or
        # missing key makes its shape wrong.
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    event_id = checkpoint_raw["event_id"]
    event_hash_value = checkpoint_raw["event_hash"]
    if not _is_int(event_id) or event_id < 0:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    if not isinstance(event_hash_value, str):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    try:
        audit.validate_checkpoint(checkpoint_raw, events)
    except audit.AuditChainError:
        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
    return {"event_id": event_id, "event_hash": event_hash_value}, events


def _verify_trust(
    trust_raw: object,
    allowlist_raw: object,
    history_raw: object,
    events: list[dict],
) -> None:
    """Validate the trust extension sections against each other and the log.

    Every section is optional (a pre-feature snapshot omits them); a present
    section is strictly validated. Field presence and raw JSON primitive types
    are input errors; value-format, ordering and uniqueness defects, and any
    disagreement between the key history, the trust registry and the audit
    log's source-key lifecycle events, are integrity errors.

    The registry is always reconciled against the event log: every registry
    source must have a complete, well-formed lifecycle (register -> rotates ->
    at most one revoke), its latest version/public key and its revoked status
    must agree with the log, and every lifecycle event must name a registry
    source — orphan sources/events and missing events are integrity failures.
    A snapshot predating ``source_key_history`` omits that one section: the
    registry/event checks still run, but there is no persisted history array to
    cross-check (the history is reconstructed in memory by the node instead).
    """
    registry = _parse_trust_sources(trust_raw)
    _parse_allowlist(allowlist_raw)
    expected = _reconstruct_key_history(registry, events)
    if history_raw is None:
        # Legacy snapshot without the section: the registry/allowlist and the
        # registry/event reconciliation above still apply, but there is no
        # persisted history array to cross-check.
        return
    history = _parse_source_key_history(history_raw)
    for source, entries in history.items():
        if source not in registry:
            # A history item whose source is absent from the registry is
            # orphan data; the persisted sections must agree bidirectionally.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if entries != expected[source]:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
    for source in registry:
        if source not in history:
            # Current snapshots write one history item per registered source.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)


def _parse_trust_sources(raw: object) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Validate the persisted source-trust registry as a raw JSON array.

    The array must be sorted by source with no duplicates; each record
    carries exactly ``{source, public_key, expires_at, version, status}``.
    A missing/extra key, a wrong primitive field type or an
    unsorted/duplicate source is an input error; an invalid public key or
    status, or a non-positive integer version, is an integrity error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return {}
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    registry: dict[str, dict] = {}
    previous: str | None = None
    for entry in raw:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if set(entry) != set(_TRUST_SOURCE_KEYS):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        source = entry["source"]
        public_key = entry["public_key"]
        expires_at = entry["expires_at"]
        version = entry["version"]
        status = entry["status"]
        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not isinstance(public_key, str):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not _is_int(expires_at):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not _is_int(version):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not isinstance(status, str):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if version < 1:
            # A structurally integer but non-positive version is a corrupt
            # value, not a wrong-shape document.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if status not in _TRUST_STATUSES:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if previous is not None and source <= previous:
            # Sources must be unique and strictly ascending; an out-of-order
            # item is a key-order (shape) defect, not a value mismatch.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        previous = source
        registry[source] = {
            "public_key": public_key,
            "expires_at": expires_at,
            "version": version,
            "status": status,
        }
    return registry


def _parse_allowlist(raw: object) -> None:
    """Validate the keyless ``{source: expires_at}`` allowlist object."""
    if raw is None:
        return
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    for source, expires_at in raw.items():
        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not _is_int(expires_at):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)


def _parse_source_key_history(raw: object) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    """Validate the persisted per-source key history structurally.

    The array must be sorted by source with no duplicates; each item is
    exactly ``{source, keys}`` with a non-empty ``keys`` list of
    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` entries whose versions are
    dense from 1 and whose activation ids are positive and strictly ascend.
    A missing/extra key, a wrong primitive field type, a duplicate/unsorted
    source, non-dense versions or non-ascending activation ids is an input
    error; an invalid public key, a non-positive version or a non-positive
    activation id is integrity.
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
    history: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    previous: str | None = None
    for item in raw:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if set(item) != set(_HISTORY_ITEM_KEYS):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        source = item["source"]
        keys = item["keys"]
        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if not isinstance(keys, list) or not keys:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        if previous is not None and source <= previous:
            # History items must be unique and source-ascending like the
            # registry they mirror; an out-of-order item is a key-order
            # (shape) defect, not a value mismatch.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
        previous = source
        entries: list[dict] = []
        for position, entry in enumerate(keys):
            if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(_HISTORY_KEY_KEYS):
                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
            version = entry["version"]
            public_key = entry["public_key"]
            activated = entry["activated_event_id"]
            if not _is_int(version):
                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
            if not isinstance(public_key, str):
                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
            if not _is_int(activated):
                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
            if version < 1:
                # A structurally integer but non-positive version is a corrupt
                # value, not a wrong-shape document.
                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
            if version != position + 1:
                # Key versions are dense from 1; an out-of-order keys item is
                # a key-order (shape) defect, not a value mismatch.
                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
            if activated < 1:
                # Every key is activated by a real, positive audit event id.
                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
            if position > 0 and activated <= entries[-1]["activated_event_id"]:
                # Activation event ids strictly ascend with the version; an
                # out-of-order keys item is a key-order (shape) defect.
                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
            entries.append(
                {
                    "version": version,
                    "public_key": public_key,
                    "activated_event_id": activated,
                }
            )
        history[source] = entries
    return history


def _reconstruct_key_history(
    registry: dict[str, dict], events: list[dict]
) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    """Rebuild the expected key histories and reconcile them with the registry.

    Mirrors ``LedgerStore._reconstruct_source_key_history`` but enforces
    *bidirectional* correspondence among the registry, the persisted history
    and the audit log:

    * every ``source_registered`` / ``source_rotated`` / ``source_revoked``
      event must name a source present in the registry (an event for an
      unknown source is an orphan event);
    * version 1 is activated by a source's single ``source_registered``
      event, each later version by the matching dense ``source_rotated``
      event, and a ``source_revoked`` event references the current key
      without adding one;
    * each registry source must have its registration (a missing event is
      fatal), the number of key events must equal its current version, the
      latest event's public key must equal the registry key, and the
      registry status is ``revoked`` exactly when a revoke event exists.

    Any malformed lifecycle payload, orphan event, missing registration,
    version gap, rotation after revocation, latest-key/version disagreement
    or revoked-status mismatch is an integrity error. Returns the
    reconstructed histories.
    """
    # Collect every source-key lifecycle event by source in log order. A
    # lifecycle event for an unknown source is validated like any other; it
    # can never be silently ignored as an orphan.
    events_by_source: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for event in events:
        kind = event.get("kind")
        if kind not in _SOURCE_KEY_EVENT_KINDS:
            continue
        source = event.get("source")
        event_id = event.get("event_id")
        public_key = event.get("public_key")
        expires_at = event.get("expires_at")
        version = event.get("version")
        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if (
            not isinstance(public_key, str)
            or not crypto.is_hex64(public_key)
            or not _is_int(expires_at)
            or not _is_int(version)
            or version < 1
            or not _is_int(event_id)
            or event_id < 1
        ):
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        events_by_source.setdefault(source, []).append(event)

    for source in events_by_source:
        if source not in registry:
            # A source-key lifecycle event with no registry record is orphan
            # data: the registry and the event log must correspond both ways.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

    reconstructed: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    for source, record in registry.items():
        entries: list[dict] = []
        revoked = False
        next_version = 1
        for event in events_by_source.get(source, ()):
            kind = event["kind"]
            event_id = event["event_id"]
            public_key = event["public_key"]
            version = event["version"]
            if kind == EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED:
                if entries or version != 1:
                    # The history opens with a single version-1 registration.
                    raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
                entries.append(
                    {
                        "version": 1,
                        "public_key": public_key,
                        "activated_event_id": event_id,
                    }
                )
                next_version = 2
            elif kind == EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED:
                if revoked or not entries or version != next_version:
                    # Rotations increment the version one step at a time and
                    # never happen after revocation.
                    raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
                entries.append(
                    {
                        "version": version,
                        "public_key": public_key,
                        "activated_event_id": event_id,
                    }
                )
                next_version = version + 1
            else:  # EVENT_SOURCE_REVOKED
                if (
                    not entries
                    or version != entries[-1]["version"]
                    or public_key != entries[-1]["public_key"]
                ):
                    # Revocation pins the current key without adding one.
                    raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
                revoked = True
        if not entries:
            # A registered source has no source_registered event.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if len(entries) != record["version"]:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if entries[-1]["public_key"] != record["public_key"]:
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        if revoked != (record["status"] == TRUST_REVOKED):
            # The registry status and the event log must agree on whether the
            # source was revoked: a revoked record without a revoke event, or
            # an active record carrying one, is corruption.
            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
        reconstructed[source] = entries
    return reconstructed

10	        "candidate": [...],           # full block list starting at genesis
11	        "proofs": [                   # optional Merkle inclusion proofs
12	            {"height": int, "proof": {height, tx_id, index, merkle_root,
13	                                      block_hash, siblings}},
14	            ...
15	        ],
16	        # Optional account-state extension: all four fields are either present
17	        # together or absent together, and state_proofs is a non-empty list.
18	        "state_root": str,            # 64 lowercase hex, anchored state root
19	        "state_height": int,          # confirmed anchor block height
20	        "state_block_hash": str,      # 64 lowercase hex anchor block hash
21	        "state_proofs": [             # account-state inclusion proofs
22	            {"height": int, "proof": {account, balance,
23	                                      confirmed_transactions, index,
24	                                      state_root, height, block_hash,
25	                                      siblings}},
26	            ...
27	        ],
28	        "signature": str,             # optional Ed25519 signature hex
29	    }
30	
31	The local trust document pins the genesis block hash and records, per source,
32	an optional Ed25519 public key with its own expiry, plus an allowlist of
33	sources accepted without signatures:
34	
35	    trust = {
36	        "genesis_hash": "<64 lowercase hex chars>",
37	        "sources": {source: {"public_key": hex, "expires_at": int}},
38	        "allowlist": {source: expires_at_int},
39	    }
40	
41	Verification, in order:
42	
43	1. **input** — bundle and trust must have the documented shape; every numeric
44	   field must be a plain (non-boolean) integer.
45	2. **auth** — the source must be trusted (a ``sources`` entry or the
46	   ``allowlist``). A source with a public key must sign the bundle; a bundle
47	   carrying a signature for a key-less source, or an unsigned bundle from a
48	   non-allowlisted source, fails.
49	3. **expired** — neither the bundle deadline nor the trust entry's deadline
50	   may have passed (``expires_at <= now`` counts as expired).
51	4. **integrity** — the signature (when required) is verified over
52	   Ed25519(sha256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle without
53	   ``signature``)); the candidate chain is recomputed from the pinned genesis
54	   (heights, prev_hash linkage, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
55	   signature, unique tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes, pending-only-at-tip)
56	   and the response's descriptor fields are checked against the recomputed
57	   tip descriptor ``S``.
58	5. **proof** — every proof must be unique, its tx_id/height/index and block
59	   fields must agree with the candidate block, the Merkle path must verify
60	   under the existing rules, and its block must not be the pending tip. When
61	   the state extension is present, its anchor (``state_height`` /
62	   ``state_block_hash``) must name a confirmed candidate block (integrity) and
63	   every state proof must agree with both anchor heights, the state root and
64	   the anchor hash; each account must sit at its ``index`` in the ascending
65	   account set of the anchor height's confirmed transactions, ``height`` +
66	   ``account`` pairs must be unique, and every proof must pass
67	   ``crypto.verify_account_proof`` against the bundle's anchors.
68	
69	On success :func:`verify_bundle` returns
70	``{"ok": True, "source", "S", "verified_tx_ids"}`` — plus
71	``"verified_accounts"`` (ascending) when the state extension was verified —
72	on failure ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
73	``input/auth/expired/integrity/proof``.
74	
75	:func:`verify_range_export` verifies one exported incremental range delivery
76	(the ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` document, top-level key order
77	``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip, attestation``)
78	offline against a caller-pinned expected anchor and the local trust document.
79	The expected anchor must strictly equal the document's ``anchor``; the
80	delivered tail is recomputed standalone from that anchor (consecutive
81	heights, prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures,
82	unique and block-ascending tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes,
83	pending-only-at-tip) and the closed ``tip`` summary must recompute. A
84	``plain`` export must come from an unexpired ``allowlist`` entry and carry
85	``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authenticated by key
86	version: when the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping,
87	the attestation's ``version`` selects that source's historical public key
88	(which must equal the attestation's ``public_key``); an unknown source or
89	version, or a mismatched key, is ``auth`` and a signature that fails to
90	verify is ``integrity`` — so an export signed under a since-rotated key
91	stays verifiable. A trust document without ``source_key_history`` keeps the
92	legacy rule: the source must be an unexpired ``trust.sources`` entry whose
93	pinned key matches the attestation and verifies the Ed25519 signature over
94	the SHA-256 digest of the canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message.
95	Failures map to ``input`` (structure), ``auth`` (authorization), ``expired``
96	(deadlines) and ``integrity`` (anchor/chain/signature); nothing is raised.
97	Success returns ``{"ok": True, "source", "request_id", "mode", "anchor",
98	"tip", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending.
99	
100	:func:`verify_range_exports` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
101	range deliveries as one continuous chain. The first page's anchor must equal
102	the caller-pinned ``expected_anchor``; every later page's anchor must equal
103	the previous page's closed tip's ``{height, block_hash}``. Each page is
104	re-verified under the same input/auth/expired/integrity rules, transaction
105	ids are unique across the whole batch, and a pending block may only appear on
106	the last page — a broken anchor, a height jump, a duplicate transaction or any
107	block after a pending one is an ``integrity`` failure. Success returns
108	``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``tip``
109	the last page's tip, ``pages`` the page count and ``verified_tx_ids``
110	ascending; failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one
111	of ``input/auth/expired/integrity``.
112	
113	:func:`advance` durably checkpoints a verified batch to ``path``. The
114	checkpoint file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with the exact declared key
115	order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash`` and a single trailing
116	newline (non-ASCII written unescaped); ``generation`` starts at 1 and
117	increments per successful advance, ``anchor``/``tip`` are the batch's pinned
118	anchor and closed tip, ``context`` has the exact key order
119	``verified_at, trust, documents, verified_tx_ids`` (the ``now`` at verification,
120	the trust document and the re-verifiable batch verbatim) and ``state_hash`` is
121	the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact) JSON of the other four fields.
122	The first advance requires a legal ``anchor``; later advances accept ``None``
123	(continue from the stored tip) or the stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``.
124	Verification itself is :func:`verify_range_exports` unchanged. Same-path
125	advances share one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a
126	failed verification never bumps the generation. An existing checkpoint is
127	strictly reloaded (key order, types, state hash and a context replay at its
128	``verified_at``); any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never
129	truncated or rebuilt. Failures return only ``{"ok": False, "error":
130	category}`` with category one of
131	``input/auth/expired/integrity/state/io``; success appends the new
132	``generation`` as the final result key.
133	"""

183	class _Failure(Exception):
184	    """Internal control-flow exception carrying the public error category."""
185	
186	    def __init__(self, category: str) -> None:
187	        self.category = category
188	        super().__init__(category)

191	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
192	    """Plain integer test; booleans are rejected (bool subclasses int)."""
193	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

196	def canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
197	    """Sorted, compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle with its signature removed.
198	
199	    This is the exact byte document whose SHA-256 the source signs, so signers
200	    and verifiers always agree regardless of incoming key order. The
201	    serialization mirrors :func:`ledger.crypto.canonical_message`: sorted keys,
202	    compact separators, UTF-8 bytes.
203	    """
204	    unsigned = {key: value for key, value in bundle.items() if key != "signature"}
205	    return json.dumps(
206	        unsigned, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
207	    ).encode("utf-8")
208	
209	
210	def bundle_signing_digest(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
211	    """The 32-byte SHA-256 digest covered by a bundle Ed25519 signature."""
212	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle)).digest()

215	def verify_bundle(bundle: object, trust: object, now: float | None = None) -> dict:
216	    """Verify an offline proof bundle against the local trust document.
217	
218	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "source": ..., "S": ..., "verified_tx_ids": [...]}``
219	    on success — extended bundles also carry ``"verified_accounts"`` — or
220	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure. Never raises for
221	    malformed input: every defect maps to one of the five categories.
222	    """
223	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
224	    try:
225	        source, candidate = _validate_inputs(bundle, trust)
226	        _authenticate(bundle, trust, source, current)
227	        blocks_raw = candidate["blocks"] if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
228	        blocks = _recompute_chain(blocks_raw, trust)
229	        descriptor = _tip_descriptor(blocks)
230	        _check_candidate_summary(candidate, descriptor)
231	        _check_response(bundle["response"], descriptor)
232	        has_state = "state_root" in bundle
233	        if has_state:
234	            _check_state_anchor(bundle, blocks)
235	        verified_ids = _verify_proofs(bundle["proofs"], blocks)
236	        verified_accounts = (
237	            _verify_state_proofs(bundle, blocks) if has_state else None
238	        )
239	    except _Failure as failure:
240	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
241	    except Exception:
242	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
243	        # crash the verifying process.
244	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
245	    result = {
246	        "ok": True,
247	        "source": source,
248	        "S": descriptor,
249	        "verified_tx_ids": verified_ids,
250	    }
251	    if verified_accounts is not None:
252	        result["verified_accounts"] = verified_accounts
253	    return result

257	
258	
259	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
260	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
261	
262	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
263	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
264	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
265	    """
266	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
267	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
268	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
269	        if field not in bundle:
270	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
271	    source = bundle["source"]
272	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
273	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
274	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
275	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
276	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
277	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
278	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
279	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
280	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
281	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
282	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
283	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
284	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
285	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
286	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
287	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
288	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
289	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
290	
291	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
292	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
293	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
294	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
295	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
296	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
297	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
298	    for name, entry in sources.items():
299	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
300	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
301	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
302	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
303	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
304	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
305	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
306	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
307	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
308	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
309	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
310	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
311	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
312	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
313	    return source, candidate
314	
315	
316	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
317	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
318	
319	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
320	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
321	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
322	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
323	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
324	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
325	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
326	    """
327	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
328	    if not present:
329	        return
330	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
331	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
332	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
333	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
334	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
335	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
336	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
337	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
338	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
339	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
340	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
341	    for item in state_proofs:
342	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
343	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
344	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
345	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
346	        proof = item["proof"]
347	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
348	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
349	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
350	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
351	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
352	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
353	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
354	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
355	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
356	        ):
357	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
358	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
359	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
360	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
361	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
362	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
363	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
364	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
365	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
366	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
367	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

370	# -- stage 2/3: trust, expiry and signature -----------------------------------
371	
372	
373	def _authenticate(
374	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
375	) -> None:
376	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
377	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
378	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
379	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
380	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
381	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
382	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
383	
384	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
385	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
386	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
387	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
388	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
389	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
390	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
391	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
392	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
393	
394	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
395	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
396	    if public_key is not None:
397	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
398	        if signature is None:
399	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
400	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
401	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
402	        ):
403	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
404	        return
405	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
406	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
407	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
408	    if signature is not None:
409	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
410

413	
414	
415	def _tip_descriptor(blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
416	    tip = blocks[-1]
417	    return {
418	        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
419	        "height": tip.height,
420	        "length": len(blocks),
421	        "status": tip.status,
422	    }

424	
425	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
426	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
427	
428	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
429	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
430	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
431	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
432	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
433	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
434	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
435	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
436	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
437	    """
438	    blocks: list[Block] = []
439	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
440	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
441	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
442	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
443	        height = block_raw.get("height")
444	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
445	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
446	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
447	        status = block_raw.get("status")
448	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
449	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
450	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
451	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
452	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
453	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
454	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
455	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
456	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
457	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
458	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
459	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
460	        if height != position:
461	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
462	        expected_prev = (
463	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
464	        )
465	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
466	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
467	        if position == 0:
468	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
469	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
470	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
471	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
472	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
473	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
474	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
475	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
476	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
477	
478	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
479	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
480	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
481	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
482	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
483	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
484	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
485	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
486	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
487	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
488	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
489	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
490	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
491	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
492	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
493	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
494	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
495	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
496	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
497	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
498	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
499	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
500	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
501	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
502	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
503	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
504	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
505	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
506	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
507	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
508	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
509	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
510	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
511	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
512	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
513	        if recomputed != block_hash:
514	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
515	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
516	        # the comparison decisions above.
517	        try:
518	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
519	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
520	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
521	    return blocks

524	def _check_candidate_summary(candidate: object, descriptor: dict) -> None:
525	    """Cross-check an export-format candidate's own tip summary fields.
526	
527	    A bare block list has nothing to check. A five-field export document's
528	    supplied ``tip_hash/height/length/status`` must equal the recomputed tip
529	    descriptor, exactly as the node requires on resubmission.
530	    """
531	    if not isinstance(candidate, dict):
532	        return
533	    for field in DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS:
534	        if field in candidate and candidate[field] != descriptor[field]:
535	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

540

542	    recomputed chain at all, so it is rejected rather than vacuously accepted.

546	        if field in response:

554	def _check_state_anchor(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
555	    """Bind the state extension's anchor to the recomputed candidate chain.
556	
557	    ``state_height`` must name a confirmed candidate block whose hash equals
558	    ``state_block_hash``; an unknown height, a pending block or a hash
559	    mismatch is an integrity failure. Every state-proof item and document
560	    must agree with both anchor heights, the bundle's state root and the
561	    anchor block hash.
562	    """
563	    height = bundle["state_height"]
564	    state_root = bundle["state_root"]
565	    block_hash = bundle["state_block_hash"]
566	    if height >= len(blocks):
567	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
568	    block = blocks[height]
569	    if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.block_hash != block_hash:
570	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
571	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
572	        proof = item["proof"]
573	        if item["height"] != height or proof["height"] != height:
574	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
575	        if proof["state_root"] != state_root or proof["block_hash"] != block_hash:
576	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

581	
582	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
583	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
584	
585	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
586	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
587	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
588	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
589	    """
590	    verified: list[str] = []
591	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
592	    for item in proofs_raw:
593	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
594	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
595	        height = item.get("height")
596	        proof = item.get("proof")
597	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
598	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
599	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
600	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
601	        block = blocks[height]
602	        if block.height != height:
603	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
604	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
605	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
606	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
607	
608	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
609	        index = proof.get("index")
610	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
611	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
612	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
613	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
614	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
615	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
616	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
617	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
618	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
619	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
620	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
621	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
622	
623	        key = (height, tx_id)
624	        if key in seen:
625	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
626	        seen.add(key)
627	
628	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
629	            tx_id,
630	            proof.get("siblings"),
631	            block.merkle_root,
632	            block.block_hash,
633	            block.block_hash,
634	        ):
635	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
636	        verified.append(tx_id)
637	    return sorted(verified)
638

640	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
641	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
642	
643	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
644	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
645	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
646	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
647	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
648	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
649	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
650	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
651	    ascending.
652	    """
653	    height = bundle["state_height"]
654	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
655	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
656	    accounts: set[str] = set()
657	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
658	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
659	            continue
660	        for tx in block.transactions:
661	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
662	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
663	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
664	
665	    verified: list[str] = []
666	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
667	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
668	        proof = item["proof"]
669	        account = proof["account"]
670	        expected = position.get(account)
671	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
672	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
673	        # failure.
674	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
675	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
676	        key = (item["height"], account)
677	        if key in seen:
678	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
679	        seen.add(key)
680	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
681	            proof,
682	            bundle["state_root"],
683	            height,
684	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
685	        ):
686	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
687	        verified.append(account)
688	    return sorted(verified)

770	def verify_range_exports(
771	    documents: object,
772	    expected_anchor: object,
773	    trust: object,
774	    now: int | float | None = None,
775	) -> dict:
776	    """Verify an ordered batch of exported range deliveries as one chain.
777	
778	    ``documents`` must be a non-empty list of decoded
779	    ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` documents (each with the exact key
780	    order ``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip,
781	    attestation``); ``expected_anchor`` is the caller-pinned
782	    ``{height, block_hash}`` the first page's anchor must strictly equal;
783	    ``trust`` is the local trust document applied to every page.
784	
785	    The pages are re-verified in order: the first page is checked against
786	    ``expected_anchor``, and every later page's anchor must strictly equal the
787	    previous page's closed ``tip`` reduced to ``{height, block_hash}`` — which
788	    also rejects a height jump or a fork at the seam. Transaction ids must be
789	    unique across the whole batch, not just inside one page, and a pending
790	    block may only appear on the last page.
791	
792	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` on
793	    success — ``anchor`` the pinned anchor of the first page, ``tip`` the last
794	    page's closed tip, ``pages`` the number of pages and
795	    ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending across every page — or
796	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure with category one of
797	    ``input/auth/expired/integrity``. Never raises for malformed input.
798	    """
799	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
800	    try:
801	        if not isinstance(documents, list) or not documents:
802	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
803	        # The pinned anchor is validated once up front so a malformed caller
804	        # anchor is an input error even before the first page is inspected.
805	        anchor = _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
806	        _validate_range_trust(trust)
807	        pages = len(documents)
808	        expected = anchor
809	        first_anchor: dict | None = None
810	        last_tip: dict | None = None
811	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
812	        verified_ids: list[str] = []
813	        for position, document in enumerate(documents):
814	            # _verify_range_page itself rejects a page whose anchor does not
815	            # strictly equal ``expected`` — the first page's pinned anchor and
816	            # every later page's previous tip — so a broken seam or a height
817	            # jump surfaces as integrity here.
818	            page_anchor, tip, page_tx_ids = _verify_range_page(
819	                document, expected, trust, current
820	            )
821	            if first_anchor is None:
822	                first_anchor = page_anchor
823	            # Transaction ids must be unique across pages, not merely within
824	            # one re-verified tail.
825	            duplicates = seen_tx_ids.intersection(page_tx_ids)
826	            if duplicates:
827	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
828	            seen_tx_ids.update(page_tx_ids)
829	            verified_ids.extend(page_tx_ids)
830	            # A pending block may only sit on the very last page: any block
831	            # delivered after a pending tip breaks the continuous confirmed
832	            # chain and cannot be linked to a committed predecessor.
833	            if tip["status"] == STATUS_PENDING and position != pages - 1:
834	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
835	            last_tip = tip
836	            expected = {"height": tip["height"], "block_hash": tip["tip_hash"]}
837	    except _Failure as failure:
838	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
839	    except Exception:
840	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
841	        # crash the verifying process.
842	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
843	    return {
844	        "ok": True,
845	        "anchor": first_anchor,
846	        "tip": last_tip,
847	        "pages": pages,
848	        "verified_tx_ids": sorted(verified_ids),
849	    }

852	def _verify_range_page(
853	    document: object, expected_anchor: object, trust: object, now: float
854	) -> tuple[dict, dict, list[str]]:
855	    """Verify one range page, returning ``(anchor, tip, verified_tx_ids)``.
856	
857	    Shared core of :func:`verify_range_export` (one page) and
858	    :func:`verify_range_exports` (a batch chaining each page's tip into the
859	    next page's expected anchor). Raises :class:`_Failure` with the public
860	    error category on every defect.
861	    """
862	    anchor = _validate_range_export_inputs(document, expected_anchor, trust)
863	    _authenticate_range_export(document, trust, now)
864	    # The caller-pinned anchor must strictly equal the delivered one.
865	    if document["anchor"] != expected_anchor:
866	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
867	    tail = _recompute_range_tail(anchor, document["blocks"])
868	    tip = _range_tip_descriptor(anchor, tail)
869	    _check_range_tip(document["tip"], tip)
870	    if document["mode"] == "attested":
871	        _verify_range_attestation(document, trust)
872	    verified_ids = sorted(tx.tx_id for block in tail for tx in block.transactions)
873	    return anchor, tip, verified_ids

876	def _validate_range_export_inputs(
877	    document: object, expected_anchor: object, trust: object
878	) -> dict:
879	    """Structural validation of the export document, the pinned anchor and
880	    the trust document. Returns the closed ``{height, block_hash}`` anchor.
881	    """
882	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
883	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
884	    if tuple(document.keys()) != RANGE_EXPORT_KEYS:
885	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
886	    source = document["source"]
887	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
888	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
889	    request_id = document["request_id"]
890	    if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
891	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
892	    if document["mode"] not in RANGE_EXPORT_MODES:
893	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
894	    if not _is_int(document["expires_at"]):
895	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
896	    anchor = _validate_range_anchor(document["anchor"])
897	    # The expected anchor is validated for shape here; the strict equality
898	    # binding itself is an integrity check after authorization and expiry.
899	    _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
900	    blocks = document["blocks"]
901	    if not isinstance(blocks, list) or not blocks:
902	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
903	    tip = document["tip"]
904	    if not isinstance(tip, dict) or set(tip) != _RANGE_TIP_KEYS:
905	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
906	    if document["mode"] == "attested":
907	        attestation = document["attestation"]
908	        if not isinstance(attestation, dict) or set(attestation) != (
909	            _RANGE_ATTESTATION_KEYS
910	        ):
911	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
912	        if not crypto.is_hex64(attestation["public_key"]):
913	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
914	        version = attestation["version"]
915	        if not _is_int(version) or version < 1:
916	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
917	        if not crypto.is_hex128(attestation["signature"]):
918	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

935	def _validate_range_trust(trust: object) -> None:
936	    """Structural validation of the trust document's ``sources``/``allowlist``.
937	
938	    Mirrors the bundle verifier's trust rules; a ``genesis_hash`` is not
939	    required here because the caller pins the range anchor directly. The
940	    optional GET /v1/trust ``source_key_history`` mapping is validated too:
941	    each source maps to a non-empty ascending array of
942	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` items whose versions are
943	    dense from 1 with strictly ascending activation ids, both numeric fields
944	    non-boolean positive integers and the public key 64 lowercase hex.
945	    """
946	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
947	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
948	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
949	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
950	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
951	    for name, entry in sources.items():
952	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
953	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
954	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
955	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
956	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
957	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
958	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
959	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
960	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
961	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
962	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
963	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
964	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
965	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
966	    history = trust.get("source_key_history")
967	    if history is not None:
968	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
969	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
970	        for name, entries in history.items():
971	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
972	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
973	            if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
974	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
975	            last_activated = None
976	            for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
977	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(
978	                    _HISTORY_ENTRY_KEYS
979	                ):
980	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
981	                version = entry.get("version")
982	                public_key = entry.get("public_key")
983	                activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
984	                # Versions are dense from 1; both numeric fields are plain
985	                # (non-boolean) positive integers.
986	                if not _is_int(version) or version != position + 1:
987	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
988	                if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
989	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
990	                if not _is_int(activated) or activated < 1:
991	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
992	                if last_activated is not None and activated <= last_activated:
993	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
994	                last_activated = activated

998	    """Whether the trust document carries a source_key_history mapping."""

1002	def _authenticate_range_export(document: dict, trust: dict, now: float) -> None:
1003	    """Check mode-specific source authorization and every deadline.
1004	
1005	    A ``plain`` export is only acceptable from an allowlisted source and must
1006	    carry ``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authorized one of
1007	    two ways:
1008	
1009	    * the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping (the new
1010	      rule): the source must appear in the mapping — the historical public key
1011	      matching and signature verification happen by attestation version in
1012	      :func:`_verify_range_attestation`; the trust ``sources`` entry and its
1013	      deadline play no role, so a delivery signed under a since-rotated or
1014	      revoked key still authenticates as long as the document itself is
1015	      unexpired;
1016	    * the mapping is absent (the legacy rule): the source must be a
1017	      ``sources`` entry whose unexpired deadline is checked.
1018	
1019	    All deadlines are checked before any integrity work: an expired,
1020	    correctly-signed export is still unusable.
1021	    """
1022	    source = document["source"]
1023	    mode = document["mode"]
1024	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1025	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1026	    if mode == "plain":
1027	        if source not in allowlist:
1028	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1029	        # A plain export carrying an attestation is not a plain delivery.
1030	        if document["attestation"] is not None:
1031	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1032	    elif _has_key_history(trust):
1033	        # Historical-key authorization: the source (and later the attestation
1034	        # version) must resolve in the mapping; the current registry entry is
1035	        # deliberately not consulted.
1036	        if source not in trust["source_key_history"]:
1037	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1038	    elif source not in sources:
1039	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1040	
1041	    if document["expires_at"] <= now:
1042	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1043	    if mode == "plain":
1044	        if allowlist[source] <= now:
1045	            raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1046	    elif not _has_key_history(trust) and sources[source]["expires_at"] <= now:
1047	        # Legacy rule only: the pinned registry entry's own deadline applies.
1048	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)

1051	def _recompute_range_tail(anchor: dict, blocks_raw: list) -> list[Block]:
1052	    """Recompute and validate the delivered tail standalone from the anchor.
1053	
1054	    Mirrors the node's own range-tail rules: heights run consecutively from
1055	    ``anchor.height + 1``, the first ``prev_hash`` is the anchor hash and
1056	    later ones link internally, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
1057	    signature verifies, tx_ids are unique across the tail and ascending
1058	    inside each block, Merkle roots and block hashes recompute, and a pending
1059	    block may only sit at the tail tip. Every field is checked on the *raw*
1060	    JSON value; type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height,
1061	    non-positive or non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while
1062	    recomputation mismatches stay ``integrity``.
1063	    """
1064	    blocks: list[Block] = []
1065	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1066	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(blocks_raw):
1067	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
1068	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1069	        height = block_raw.get("height")

1097	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
1098	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):

1101	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
1102	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
1103	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
1104	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")

1106	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
